ACCPPDE101.name: Personal & Professional Development
ACCPPDE101.topics: Scholarly sources and research questions; Argumentation and thesis statements; Literature synthesis; Academic integrity and referencing; Community engagement; Personal learning goals and reflective learning; Collaborative learning; Self-efficacy; Stress and time management; Responsible use of AI

ENSGATE101.name: Sustainability Essentials I
ENSGATE101.contribution: Introduces physical and quantitative principles used to examine sustainability systems.
ENSGATE101.topics: Planetary boundaries and the Anthropocene; Exponential growth and environmental change; Graphs, rates and uncertainty; Dynamic systems; Chemical bonds, reactions and equilibria; Ocean acidification and nutrient cycles; Thermodynamics and entropy; Greenhouse gases and energy; Ozone depletion; Newtonian mechanics, stress and strain; Biopolymers and material properties

ENSENVI111.name: Dynamic Earth
ENSENVI111.contribution: Studies interacting lithosphere and hydrosphere processes through Earth science and field labs.
ENSENVI111.topics: Plate tectonics and the Wilson cycle; Minerals and rock formation; Volcanism and metamorphism; Sedimentation and facies; Structural deformation; Stratigraphy and palaeontology; Seismology and seismic waves; Geomagnetism and gravity; Mantle and core processes; Earth-system and climate interactions; Geological history; Geohazards

BENECON111.name: Introduction to Economics
BENECON111.contribution: Introduces incentives, markets and scarcity for evaluating environmental choices.
BENECON111.topics: Supply and demand; Game theory; Rational consumer choice; Individual and market demand; Production and costs; Perfect competition; Aggregate output; Unemployment and inflation; Goods and financial markets; IS-LM model

ENSGATE201.name: Sustainability Essentials II
ENSGATE201.contribution: Applies sustainability analysis to an interdisciplinary real-world case.
ENSGATE201.topics: Electromagnetic and mechanical waves; Wave composition and interference; Optical spectroscopy; Electron microscopy; Inorganic and organic chemistry; Chemical testing; Material structure and crystallography; Stress and strain; Sustainable material design; Geological wave applications; Nuclear power and waste; Greenwashing

BENGATE102.name: Research Methods & Statistics
BENGATE102.contribution: Introduces quantitative research design and statistics for economic or environmental evidence.
BENGATE102.topics: Scientific inquiry and hypotheses; Operationalization and measurement; Reliability and validity; Survey construction and sampling; Randomized and quasi-experimental designs; Nonexperimental and qualitative research; Descriptive statistics; Sampling distributions and estimation; Hypothesis testing and confidence intervals; Association and regression; Research ethics and anonymous data collection

ENSENVI112.name: Natural Hazards, Risks & Adaptations
ENSENVI112.contribution: Analyses natural hazards, exposure, climate-driven risks and adaptation measures.
ENSENVI112.topics: Covers geoscience principles and analytical tools to understand natural disasters. Compares risks from climate change‑driven events and mining disasters and teaches actions to reduce risks from events like earthquakes, droughts and toxic algae blooms.

DISGATE102.name: Mathematical Methods
DISGATE102.contribution: Supplies calculus and linear algebra for quantitative modelling of systems.
DISGATE102.topics: Functions and limits; Continuity; Differentiation; Optimization; Taylor series; Complex numbers; Definite and indefinite integrals; Integration techniques; First-order differential equations; Population-growth and predator–prey models; Second-order linear differential equations; Dynamic models

ENSSUST111.name: Climate Change
ENSSUST111.contribution: Examines climate drivers, impacts and adaptation, including sea-level rise.
ENSSUST111.topics: Anthropogenic climate change; Greenhouse gases; Feedback loops and tipping points; Ocean acidification and sea-level rise; Biosphere impacts; Agriculture, transport and construction; Climate and health; Climate justice and governance; Paris Agreement; Renewable energy and sustainable heat; Carbon removal and geoengineering; Climate communication and misinformation; Climate anxiety; Mitigation and adaptation

ENSDELT111.name: Building with Nature
ENSDELT111.contribution: Uses nature-based coastal engineering, flood protection and land-reclamation cases to study adaptation options.
ENSDELT111.topics: Nature-based infrastructure; Coastal and water management; Walcheren's water-management history; Sandy and muddy coasts; Lowland lakes; Rivers and estuaries; Urban nature-based solutions; Harbour habitats; Habitat connectivity; Ecoducts and fish ladders

ENSECOL111.name: Introduction to Biodiversity
ENSECOL111.contribution: Introduces biodiversity patterns, ecological interactions, threats and conservation as scientific foundations for sustainability.
ENSECOL111.topics: Biodiversity and its measurement; Phylogenetic relationships; Viruses; Bacteria and archaea; Protists; Fungi; Plant diversity; Invertebrates; Vertebrates and primates; Evolutionary history; Organismal ecological roles

DISDATA111.name: Introduction to Data Science
DISDATA111.contribution: Works with and visualises spatial datasets as evidence for interdisciplinary inquiry.
DISDATA111.topics: Data visualization; Exploratory data analysis; Tidy data; Data transformation and integration; Dates and times; Web data; Text data; Geospatial data; Programming functions; Data-based research questions

ENSENVI211.name: Earth Observation
ENSENVI211.contribution: Uses GIS, satellite and drone data to investigate environmental change.
ENSENVI211.topics: Spatial concepts and data models; Geospatial databases; Georeferencing and map projections; Spatial visualization; Spatial queries and transformations; Surface analysis; Earth-observation tools; Spectral signatures; Remote-sensing acquisition systems; Image preprocessing and processing; Environmental geospatial applications

ENSENVI212.name: Soils & Aquifers
ENSENVI212.contribution: Studies soils and aquifers with field and laboratory analysis relevant to water resources and coastal defence.
ENSENVI212.topics: Soil formation, functions and taxonomy; Soil quality, amendments and threats; Soil texture, structure and aggregate stability; Soil moisture and organic matter; Soil chemistry, pH and metals; Soil biology; Sediment-cell behaviour; Shallow aquifers, salinization and freshwater interventions; Physical and geophysical properties of soils and aquifers; Seismology; Electrical resistivity; Electromagnetic surveying

BENECON212.name: Microeconomics & Behavior
BENECON212.contribution: Analyses choice under scarcity and regulation, grounding economic evaluation of resource use.
BENECON212.topics: Choice under uncertainty; Non-egoistic preferences; Cognitive limitations; Monopoly; Imperfect competition and strategic behaviour; Labour markets; Capital markets; General equilibrium; Market efficiency; Externalities; Government intervention

ENSDELT211.name: Living with Water
ENSDELT211.contribution: Studies flood, sea-level and subsidence adaptation through delta water-management projects.
ENSDELT211.topics: Delta environments; Flood risk and protection; Drainage and freshwater management; Sea-level rise and subsidence; Salinization; Water infrastructure and ecological consequences; Water governance, law and justice; Contaminants and pollution; EU Water Framework Directive; Nature-based adaptation; Urban ecology and water; Long-term delta resilience

ENSENVI311.name: Environmental Biogeochemistry
ENSENVI311.contribution: Models water–rock–soil cycles and resource recovery in a geochemical case.
ENSENVI311.topics: Natural-water composition; Chemical equilibrium and ionic activity; Aqueous speciation and complexation; Mineral saturation, precipitation and dissolution; Carbonate equilibria, alkalinity and buffering; Ocean acidification; Redox processes and microbial controls; Adsorption and mineral surfaces; Weathering and clay formation; Biomineralization; Contaminant transport; Environmental remediation and resource recovery

ENSDELT311.name: R3: Recycling, Recovery, Remediation
ENSDELT311.contribution: Examines circular-economy recovery technologies, material stewardship and resource security.
ENSDELT311.topics: Circular resource supply; Solar-cell and solar-panel recycling; Delamination and material separation; Electronic waste; Pyrometallurgy and hydrometallurgy; Precious-metal recovery; Plastic-recycling legislation; Phytoremediation; Mycoremediation; Mycelium-based soil amendments

DISMATH314.name: Probability & Statistics
DISMATH314.contribution: Provides probability and statistical inference for quantitative environmental evidence.
DISMATH314.topics: Probability spaces and conditional probability; Random variables and expectation; Moment-generating functions; Discrete and continuous distributions; Multivariate and conditional distributions; Transformations and correlation; Sampling and order statistics; Confidence intervals and hypothesis tests; Estimation efficiency; Bayesian inference; Monte Carlo methods

ENSSUST313.name: Research in a Sustainable Delta
ENSSUST313.contribution: Small teams investigate regionally situated sustainability questions supplied by external organizations, developing research questions, plans and evidence.
ENSSUST313.topics: Regionally situated sustainability problems; Research-question development; Research planning; Academic literature and evidence; External stakeholder collaboration; Applied sustainability investigation

ENSENVI312.name: Earth's Resources
ENSENVI312.contribution: Researches geoscience of geothermal energy, waste storage and carbon capture.
ENSENVI312.topics: Provides in‑depth geoscience research into resource and environmental challenges such as nuclear waste storage, geothermal energy and CO₂ capture. Students conduct literature reviews and produce class reports for presentation to a professional conference.

ENSDELT312.name: Governance of Sustainability
ENSDELT312.contribution: Evaluates how government and non-government stakeholders shape sustainability policy.
ENSDELT312.topics: Institutions, actors and power; Collective action and common-pool resources; Governance modes and networks; Techno-optimism and ecological limits; Climate justice; Populism and environmental politics; Wicked and long-term problems; Public participation; Food, water and energy governance; Markets, public goods and externalities; Adaptive and global governance; Climate mitigation; Policy effectiveness and feasibility

BENECON312.name: Econometrics
BENECON312.contribution: Develops causal and predictive empirical analysis of economic data; environmental application is a possible project, not course-specific.
BENECON312.topics: Econometrics supplies tools to analyze data to answer questions of causality and prediction. In this course you learn three estimators—Ordinary Least Squares, Generalized Least Squares, and Instrumental Variables—and three tests—t-test, F-test, and LM-test. Understanding the basic rules of econometrics, particularly the sampling distribution concept, is key, and the course uses Monte Carlo simulations in Stata to visualize it. Tools are applied to estimate economic relationships and make predictions, and students write an empirical paper.

GOSSOCI215.name: Social Movements & Environmental Justice
GOSSOCI215.contribution: Examines environmental justice movements and the social distribution of environmental costs.
GOSSOCI215.topics: Focuses on social movement theories and environmental justice. Uses case studies from the Environmental Justice Atlas and integrates perspectives such as feminism, anti‑colonialism, degrowth and environmental peacebuilding to encourage civic engagement.

ENSENVI213.name: Earth System Science Tools
ENSENVI213.contribution: Models interactions among Earth spheres with climate proxies and a field trip.
ENSENVI213.topics: Explores interactions among biosphere, hydrosphere, lithosphere and atmosphere. Teaches system modelling, uses proxies and isotope tracers to study past and future climates and includes a field trip focused on greenhouse gas pathways.

BENECON311.name: Public Economics
BENECON311.contribution: Studies public goods, externalities, taxation and welfare effects of policy, applicable to environmental decisions.
BENECON311.topics: Role and size of government; Market efficiency and failure; Public goods; Externalities; Efficiency and equity; Public production; Public choice; Public expenditure; Health and education policy; Welfare programs; Social insurance; Taxation and redistribution

DISDATA211.name: Machine Learning
DISDATA211.contribution: Develops predictive methods for datasets; environmental spatial applications would need a selected project.
DISDATA211.topics: Prediction and model accuracy; Regression and classification; Resampling and validation; Model selection and regularization; High-dimensional data; Nonlinear regression; Tree-based learning; Support vector methods; Dimension reduction; Unsupervised learning; Feature engineering

ENSSUST311.name: Renewable System Design
ENSSUST311.contribution: Designs lower-carbon energy systems with technical and economic assessment.
ENSSUST311.topics: Teaches assessment of energy usage patterns and strategies for reducing consumption or transitioning to cleaner energy. Explores solar, wind and bioenergy solutions and includes technical and economic analysis; students deliver a report and presentation to a partner company.

ENSECOL212.name: Ecosystems Uncovered: How Nature Works
ENSECOL212.contribution: Studies ecosystem dynamics, ecological modelling and applied cases.
ENSECOL212.topics: Ecology and evolution; Environmental conditions and resources; Climate and life cycles; Ecological niches; Competition and cohabitation; Predation and food webs; Natural selection; Population dynamics; Biodiversity patterns; Ecological succession; Ecosystem energy and matter fluxes; Global cycles; Conservation and human impacts; Ecosystem value

BENECON211.name: International Macroeconomics
BENECON211.contribution: Examines aggregate economic growth and policy conditions for large-scale energy transitions.
BENECON211.topics: Goods and financial markets; Labour markets; Phillips curve; IS-LM and IS-LM-PC models; Economic growth; Saving and capital accumulation; Technological progress; Expectations; Open-economy macroeconomics; Fiscal and monetary policy; Business cycles and economic crises

BENECON314.name: Behavioral Economics
BENECON314.contribution: Investigates biases and behavioural incentives that affect resource-use decisions.
BENECON314.topics: This course integrates insights from psychology into economic theory to better understand how people make decisions. Learn how actual behavior deviates from the predictions of traditional economic models due to biases, heuristics, and framing. Through experiments, students will deepen their understanding of decision-making and its implications for economic theory and practice.

options.label: Integrated Sustainability Science
options.concept: Combine Earth systems, climate and ecology with economics, governance and environmental justice. Statistics and spatial data support environmental analysis, and a team project introduces research on a regional sustainability question.

options.label: Climate Resilience and Spatial Environmental Data
options.concept: Study climate hazards, soils, groundwater, delta water management and nature-based adaptation. Use spatial observations and machine learning to investigate environmental change, with public economics to assess policy choices.

options.label: Resources, Energy and Sustainability Policy
options.concept: Study resource extraction, material recovery and renewable energy systems alongside economics and governance. Examine how policy and markets shape the use of resources and the costs and benefits of energy transitions.

analysis: The integrated option gives environmental justice and delta-water questions weight alongside biodiversity and methods. Climate resilience emphasizes Earth System Science Tools, machine learning and water hazards. The resource route adds ecosystem analysis, energy design and behavioral economics, and omits the hazards, soils and water-management sequence. All retain their 24 courses. The partner research project can run only in term 1 and has no workbook prerequisite. It provides an early introduction followed by later methodological development, unlike Leiden’s project after its formal research prerequisites. The UCR comparison does not reproduce Leiden’s interdisciplinary food system, field or thesis sequence.

alignment.rationale: Both introduce integrated sustainability questions; the UCR gateway is broader and course-sized.
Both introduce ecology and biodiversity in the context of sustainability.
Both introduce interacting Earth systems and human pressures.
Both address climate change and societal consequences; UCR emphasizes physical and sustainability dimensions.
Both analyse ecosystems and biodiversity; UCR does not reproduce the Leiden livelihoods module.
Both model environmental systems. Leiden focuses on economy–environment interactions, including input-output and material-flow models.
Both develop field-based environmental evidence, though UCR focuses on soils and aquifers.
Both study how environmental costs and benefits are distributed. UCR focuses on social movements and environmental justice, while Leiden takes an anthropological approach.
Both examine relations among science, technology and societal transitions.
Both study actors, institutions and policy choices in sustainability governance.
Leiden applies psychology to environmental behavior.
Leiden combines food-system ecology with food policy and governance.
Leiden studies climate mitigation policy through peatland carbon cases.
Both address pollution, material flows and power; UCR focuses on circular delta systems.
Both support reflection and academic development, but Leiden’s Learning My Way is programme-specific.
Both provide mathematical foundations for quantitative sustainability work.
Both teach social-science research design and statistics.
Both introduce programming and data analysis; UCR is not sustainability-specific.
Both develop statistical reasoning.
Both use empirical tools to address economic questions. Leiden applies them specifically to evaluating social and environmental policy.
Both use team inquiry into a problem supplied by an external organization. Leiden’s required consultancy course develops and presents a project plan.
Programme-specific second-year Learning My Way unit.
The genuine 30-EC minor/elective/exchange space remains student-selected and is not a fixed external course to align.
The compulsory independent 18-EC thesis cannot be counted as an ordinary UCR course or UCR’s optional research element.
Programme-specific third-year Learning My Way unit.
Leiden prepares students for the thesis through a dedicated sequence on research questions and design.
